section_summary.extract_value: This section reports intraclass correlations (ICCs) and within- and between-person correlations for the study variables, noting ICCs for exposure to body-focused and non-body-focused others (.50 and .44) and for body appreciation (.77). Within-person correlations were generally null for relations between exposures and criteria, whereas between-persons analyses showed that higher mean exposure to non-body-focused others related to higher intuitive eating, and higher mean exposure to body-focused others related to lower intuitive eating and body appreciation (p < .10) and higher dietary restraint. The section references Table 1 for detailed correlations and does not label multiple studies (no 'Study 1' or similar).
section_summary.evidence_source: Intraclass correlations (ICCs) were computed for all study variables (see Table 1). The ICCs for exposure to body focused others and exposure to non-body focused others were .50 and .44, respectively. As reported elsewhere (Kelly & Stephen, 2016), ICCs for criteria variables ranged from .56 (dietary restraint) to .77 (body appreciation). Within- and between-persons correlations between study variables are presented in Table 1... At the between-persons level, a higher mean level of exposure to non-body focused others was associated with higher mean levels of intuitive eating, over the week. A higher mean level of exposure to body focused others was associated with lower mean levels of intuitive eating and body appreciation (p < .10), and higher mean levels of dietary restraint.
